name: Butternut and chickpea curry
summary: Butternut and chickpeas simmered in a tomato curry warmed with cinnamon, cardamom and cumin, with spinach stirred through, over brown rice with a fresh tomato sambal.
about: Warming a curry with cinnamon and cardamom alongside cumin and coriander, and serving it with a fresh tomato and onion sambal, is the Cape Malay way. Butternut and chickpeas make it a meat-free supper, and the leftovers keep well for the next day's lunch.

ingredients.name: Butternut
ingredients.note: peeled, seeded and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Put the rice, 625 ml water and ½ tsp salt in a saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 40 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. Leave covered off the heat until you serve.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cinnamon, cardamom and cumin seeds and fry for about 30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the onions and fry, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin, ground turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 1 minute, until the spices darken slightly and the oil turns yellow; turn the heat down if they start to catch.

Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, until they start to break down, then add the butternut, 375 ml water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 to 18 minutes, until the butternut is tender when pierced but still holds its shape.

Stir in the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until the sauce has thickened and coats the butternut. Add the spinach and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until wilted, then stir in the garam masala. Taste for salt and take out the cinnamon stick.
While the curry simmers, mix the tomatoes, red onion, coriander and lemon juice for the sambal and season with salt.
Serve the curry over the rice with the sambal spooned on top.
prepNote: The curry keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen; make the sambal fresh.
